study.question: Does preserving feedback-specific item content as separately addressable temporal memory rescue association information that was ineffective when fused into the same relation tokens?
study.hypothesis: Observed: g0-r0010-feedback_bound macro AUC 0.8298094592 is below factorized 0.8299991984 and zero 0.8299692427. The factorized gain over zero is only 0.0000299557, with no seed evidence. Code inspection shows four action-specific projected summaries are summed into the same 35 relation/time tokens before a single JointBlock. Provisional mechanism: early fusion may prevent content-dependent access to distinct feedback histories. A separate 20-slot memory, read by inherited field/relation tokens before that JointBlock, may expose useful association beyond rates and generic extra attention. This is a discriminating follow-up to a failed association implementation, not an established limitation or a preselected winner.

nearest_work.difference: Original primary PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.11565v1 inspected directly, section3.1 Eq5 and section3.2 Eq8-11. Behavior-type pooling and cross-attention proxies are prior work. Here add a single one-way residual memory read from target-weighted global/quartile feedback item summaries into incumbent field/relation tokens; no raw event-token interaction stack, PGUs, learned task proxy predictions, or full INFNet reproduction. Priority/originality unverified.

Pinned commit90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d forward123-169 constructs four feedback-mask hubs via task-specific projection plus masked average pooling. Here shared item-summary projection, explicit counts, ordinal bins, strict key masking, and original field/relation query tokens; no per-task hub projection or separate task readout. No local effectiveness claimed for INFNet.

Retain target local activation and released-field adaptation. The memory changes representation access after target-weighted pooling, not the DIN weight mechanism. Original paper excerpt read, plus local baseline implementation inspected.

Pinned forward/tokenizer117-197 retains projected individual events with field/target tokens. This study retains compact pooled memory, with no direct event self-attention or window kernel. It cannot refute that alternative.

Pinned forward112-158 mixes globally pooled history and field group tokens. This uses addressable feedback/time memory in addition to existing relation tokens; no reversible token mixing or group tokenizer adopted.

inherited_components: All g0-r0010-feedback_factorized architecture/configuration and frozen information boundary
Shared feature embeddings, DIN local activation, raw static and global-history readouts, 35 relation-by-time summary tokens and counts
Linear rank moments and existing zero-start residual/relation/content/feedback projection banks

study.proposed_difference: Append a shared FeedbackMemory module after inherited initialization inside fork_rng. For bin t and feedback a, compute H[t,a]=sum(T[t,l]*m[a,l]*w[l]*item[l])/sqrt(7), F[t,a]=(sum(T*m_a)/max(1,sum(T)))*sum(T*w*item)/sqrt(7). Source chooses H or F; separate keeps four vectors, collapsed broadcasts their arithmetic mean over a. Collapse preserves summed content. All arms retain each feedback log1p(count)/log(101), identity, temporal validity and 20 positions. Project [content,count] to32, add bin/action identities; existing valid field/relation tokens query this memory through strictly masked 2-head cross-attention. Zero-start output projection adds a residual before the unchanged JointBlock; no tower widening. Same summaries and parameterized operations in all four arms. Added nominal parameters=8000 (shared input map3136, identities640, two LayerNorms128, four bias-free32x32 maps4096).
predictions: If feedback-content association is useful specifically when separately accessible, joint_separate should exceed factorized_separate and joint_collapsed; the association contrast should be larger under separate than collapsed layout. Predeclared interaction D=(AUC_JS-AUC_FS)-(AUC_JC-AUC_FC)>0; report all four cells even when D disagrees with overall selection.
If only marginal counts, generic residual capacity or extra attention help, factorized cells may match or exceed joint; that would not support a binding mechanism.

At initialization all four arms should exactly match the incumbent output in the same precision because the added output map is zero. Empty histories have exactly zero new residual even after learning. All cells have identical nominal parameter counts and memory masks.

Long-history slices may offer more heterogeneous feedback content, but slice differences remain exploratory with positive/negative counts; empty and rare auxiliary slices cannot establish significance.
falsifiers: Joint_separate does not outperform factorized_separate and joint_collapsed on validation macro AUC, or the predeclared interaction is nonpositive: no support for a separation-dependent association rescue in this implementation.
All variants improve similarly, or only factorized improves: attribute any measured gain to an unresolved generic memory/rate effect, not binding.

Only one frozen training seed in this proposal; small differences are preliminary; no bootstrap interface or predictions supplied
The incumbent still carries action embeddings and factorized relation-feedback information; effects estimate incremental value, not total feedback utility
Historical action masks may overlap. Rank bins are ordinal, not elapsed time. Rare feedback support is not yet measured in raw inputs
Zero output initialization delays gradient to new input/query/key/value weights; one-pass failure may be underoptimization.
Absolute norm/cross-feedback covariance differences and shared sparse feedback support can affect optimization.
The fixed host seed and cumulative validation search can yield winner selection noise. No test feedback or imported old campaigns can resolve it.
